name: KPISummary
intent: A responsive grid of MetricCard tiles driven by a single metrics[] array — the reusable KPI summary band above a dashboard, list, or report.
when: Show a row/grid of headline metrics above a page (workforce, safety, quality, etc.)
You were about to hand-roll a grid of metric Cards
Several MetricCards should share one responsive layout
whenNot: A single metric -> use MetricCard directly

A compact one-line stat bar with inline numbers and dots (e.g. core-org-overview's KPIStrip) -> that is a different shape; KPISummary is a CARD grid, not a bar (a future KPIBar widget would cover that)
Metric tiles that need a progress bar, multiple severity badges, or other bespoke content beyond MetricCard's contract -> keep those tiles bespoke until MetricCard grows those options

chooseOver.because: KPISummary owns the responsive grid and renders MetricCard tiles from data, so dashboards don't re-implement the layout.
MetricCard is one tile; KPISummary lays out many in a responsive grid.

metrics.note: One MetricCard per entry: { title, value, unit?, subtitle?, trend?, trendLabel?, icon?, status? }. The caller computes/aggregates the values.

dataContract.note: Presentational and stateless — no data fetching. Composes MetricCard for each entry.

columns.note: Columns at the lg breakpoint; responsive (1 col mobile, 2 at md).

children.note: Optional bespoke tile(s) rendered as the LAST grid cell(s), after the metric tiles — for a tile that exceeds MetricCard's contract (e.g. a multi-badge severity breakdown). Each child occupies one grid cell, so the row stays uniform. Keeps MetricCard simple.

states.default: A responsive grid (1 / 2 / N columns) of MetricCard tiles.
states.with-trailing-tile: children render as the last grid cell(s) after the metrics — a bespoke tile sits in the same row as the MetricCards.
states.empty: metrics=[] renders an empty grid (no tiles). Callers should guard if a placeholder is wanted.
states.single: One metric renders a single tile (prefer MetricCard directly in that case).

allowedPlacement: KPI band above a dashboard / list / report
forbiddenPlacement: as a compact one-line stat bar (use a KPIBar-style widget)
inside another grid that already sets columns

commonMistakes.mistake: Using KPISummary for a compact inline stat bar
commonMistakes.symptom: A card grid where a thin one-line bar was intended
commonMistakes.fix: KPISummary is a card grid; for a compact bar (numbers + dots in one row) keep/author a separate KPIBar widget.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forcing a tile with multiple badges (or other rich content) into the metrics[] contract
commonMistakes.fix: Pass that tile via the `children` trailing slot as a bespoke Card; metrics[] stays MetricCard-shaped.

commonMistakes.mistake: Baking a domain type into the metrics
commonMistakes.symptom: The grid can't be reused across pages
commonMistakes.fix: Pass generic MetricCardProps; let each page map its domain data to metrics[].

evaluationCriteria.check: KPISummary chosen for a grid of metric tiles; MetricCard for one tile; a KPIBar for a compact bar.
metrics[] is a non-empty array of MetricCardProps; no domain type baked in.
Renders one MetricCard per metric inside a responsive grid (does not re-implement the tile).
Produces a grid with one tile per metric.

notes: promotedFrom: the repeated hand-rolled KPI-strip pattern (core-project-quality-issues, core-project-workforce-safety) — a grid of metric Cards.

refactored: ["core-project-workforce-safety: KPI strip -> <KPISummary> container (3 metrics + the multi-badge 'Active Alerts' tile via the children trailing slot). Minor restyle: per-tile Progress bars dropped, their % retained in the subtitle.","core-project-quality-issues: KPI strip -> <KPISummary> container (3 metrics + the multi-badge 'Open Issues' tile via the children slot — that tile reordered to last)."]
notAdoptedBy: core-org-overview / Dashboard kpi-strip — that is a compact horizontal stat bar, a DIFFERENT shape; KPISummary (card grid) does not resolve it. A separate KPIBar widget would.
